newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori's popularity soars on Peru rescue raid.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori's popularity soars on Peru rescue raid.

text.p: The popularity of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori soared following the successful hostage rescue mission at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, a new poll showed on Saturday.
Approval ratings for Fujimori shot up from 45 percent on the day before Tuesday's raid, to 74 percent two days after, according to the Datum International survey published in El Comercio newspaper.

The poll, based on 300 interviews, showed the percentage of respondents who disapproved of Fujimori dropping to 21, from 53 before the explosive assault that freed all but one of the 72 hostages held by Marxist rebels for 126 days.
Fujimori has traditionally based much of his popular support on a tough line against Peru's leftist guerrilla groups.
A separate question showed that while only 46 percent of respondents favoured the use of force to end the hostage standoff before the raid, 85 percent said they were in favour afterwards.
No margin of error for the poll was given, nor was it revealed where the interviews were carried out.
